lead: A continuous crystallizer does not make crystals of one size. New nuclei appear all the time and each crystal grows for as long as it happens to stay in the vessel, so the product has a spread of sizes, the crystal size distribution (CSD). The CSD decides how the product filters, washes, flows and sells. The MSMPR model (mixed suspension, mixed product removal) turns a population balance into one straight-line plot that gives the growth rate, the nucleation rate and the whole CSD from a single sieve analysis.
prereq: You need nucleation, growth and the ΔL law from Nucleation and crystal growth.

blocks.text: A sieve analysis gives the mass of crystals between pairs of sieve openings. It is plotted as the cumulative mass fraction undersize against size, or converted to numbers. The basic measure for the model is the population density n = ΔN/ΔL: the number of crystals per unit size range per unit volume of magma, in number/(m³ mm). A mass ΔM on a size band of mean size L and width ΔL contains ΔN = ΔM/(ρkvL³) crystals, so n = ΔM/(ρkvL³ΔL).

The moments of n(L) give the totals: ∫n dL is the number of crystals, ∫nL² dL times ka their surface and ∫nL³ dL times ρkv their mass. Sizes are summed up by a mean (number mean, or the mass-weighted mean), by the dominant size LD where the mass distribution peaks, and by the spread, the coefficient of variation.

Assumptions: steady state; the magma is perfectly mixed, so every point has the same supersaturation and CSD; the product is withdrawn with the same CSD as the vessel; the feed holds no crystals; there is no breakage or agglomeration; and growth obeys the ΔL law, G independent of L.

Take a magma volume V and the crystals between sizes L and L + ΔL. In a time Δt, crystals grow into the band across L, GnVΔt, and out of it across L + ΔL, (Gn)<sub>L+ΔL</sub>VΔt; the product stream Q removes nQΔLΔt. At steady state in = out. Dividing by ΔLΔt and letting ΔL → 0 gives V G dn/dL = −Qn. With the residence time τ = V/Q:
dn/dL = −n/(Gτ)   ⇒   n = n° e<sup>−L/(Gτ)</sup>      ln n = ln n° − L/(Gτ)
blocks.where: n° is the population density of nuclei (L → 0), G the linear growth rate and τ the mean residence time. A plot of ln n against L is a straight line of slope −1/(Gτ) and intercept ln n°. The nucleation rate is B° = n°G (nuclei per m³ per unit time).

N<sub>T</sub> is the number of crystals per unit volume, M<sub>T</sub> the magma density (mass of crystals per unit volume; use n° per metre with L in metres), k<sub>v</sub> the volume shape factor and ρ the crystal density. The number mean size is Gτ, the dominant (peak-mass) size 3Gτ, the mass-weighted mean 4Gτ and the mass median 3.67Gτ.

blocks.text: With x = L/(Gτ), the mass fraction of product finer than L is W(x) = 1 − e<sup>−x</sup>(1 + x + x²/2 + x³/6). Every MSMPR product has the same shape of distribution, with a coefficient of variation of 50 % by mass; only Gτ, the scale, can be changed.

Plotting ln B° against ln G from runs at several residence times gives the kinetic order i in B° = k<sub>N</sub>G<sup>i</sup>, with i = b/g. If the magma density is fixed by the feed, M<sub>T</sub> ∝ G<sup>i−1</sup>(Gτ)<sup>4</sup>, which gives G ∝ τ<sup>−4/(i+3)</sup> and L<sub>D</sub> ∝ τ<sup>(i−1)/(i+3)</sup>. With i > 1, a longer residence time (lower supersaturation) gives larger crystals, but only weakly: for i = 3, doubling τ raises L<sub>D</sub> by 2<sup>1/3</sup> = 1.26.

To design, choose τ and read G and B° from the kinetics; the vessel volume is Qτ. A plot that curves upward at small sizes shows fines from breakage or size-dependent growth; one that curves downward at large sizes shows classified removal of product. Fines destruction and classified product removal are deliberately used to move away from the MSMPR distribution and narrow the product.

examples.question: An MSMPR crystallizer for ammonium sulfate (ρ = 1770 kg/m³, k<sub>v</sub> = 1) has τ = 2.0 h. A sample gives population densities n = 1.84 × 10<sup>9</sup>, 6.77 × 10<sup>8</sup>, 2.49 × 10<sup>8</sup> and 9.16 × 10<sup>7</sup> per (m³ mm) at L = 0.2, 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8 mm. Find G, n°, B°, N<sub>T</sub>, M<sub>T</sub> and L<sub>D</sub>.
steps: ln n = 21.33, 20.33, 19.33 and 18.33. Each 0.2 mm step lowers ln n by 1.00, so the slope is −5.00 per mm.
Intercept: ln n° = 21.33 + 5.00 × 0.2 = 22.33, so n° = 5.0 × 10<sup>9</sup> per (m³ mm).
B° = n°G = 5.0 × 10<sup>9</sup> × 0.100 = 5.0 × 10<sup>8</sup> nuclei per m³ per h. N<sub>T</sub> = n°Gτ = 5.0 × 10<sup>9</sup> × 0.200 = 1.0 × 10<sup>9</sup> crystals per m³.
L<sub>D</sub> = 3Gτ = 0.60 mm; number mean 0.20 mm; mass-weighted mean 0.80 mm.
examples.answer: G = 0.10 mm/h, n° = 5.0 × 10<sup>9</sup> per (m³ mm), B° = 5.0 × 10<sup>8</sup> per (m³ h), N<sub>T</sub> = 1.0 × 10<sup>9</sup> per m³, M<sub>T</sub> = 85 kg/m³, L<sub>D</sub> = 0.60 mm.

examples.question: For the same crystallizer (Gτ = 0.20 mm), what mass fraction of the product is coarser than 1.0 mm, and what fraction is finer than 0.2 mm? What size divides the product mass in half?
steps: The mass median is at x = 3.67: L = 3.67 × 0.20 = 0.73 mm.
examples.answer: 26.5 % of the mass is coarser than 1.0 mm, 1.9 % finer than 0.2 mm, and the mass median is 0.73 mm. Most crystals by number are small, yet they carry little of the mass.

traps: The slope of ln n against L is −1/(Gτ), not −G. Divide Gτ by τ to get G.
Mix units and M<sub>T</sub> is wrong by powers of 1000: use n° per metre and Gτ in metres together.
The dominant size is 3Gτ, by mass. The number mean is only Gτ, because small crystals are most numerous.
Lowering supersaturation at a fixed residence time lowers G and so lowers 3Gτ; bigger crystals come from a longer τ (bigger vessel or slower feed), and then only weakly.
The model needs a crystal-free feed and no breakage; a curved ln n plot means one of the assumptions fails.

quiz.q: What do the letters MSMPR stand for, and what are its main assumptions?
quiz.a: Mixed suspension, mixed product removal: steady state, perfect mixing, product withdrawn with the vessel's CSD, crystal-free feed, no breakage or agglomeration, and size-independent growth.

quiz.q: Derive n = n° exp(−L/Gτ) for an MSMPR crystallizer.
quiz.a: Balance on crystals between L and L + ΔL in volume V: growth in GnVΔt, growth out (Gn)<sub>L+ΔL</sub>VΔt, withdrawal QnΔLΔt. At steady state V[(Gn)<sub>L</sub> − (Gn)<sub>L+ΔL</sub>] = QnΔL; as ΔL → 0 and with G constant, dn/dL = −n/(Gτ), τ = V/Q, which integrates to n = n° exp(−L/Gτ).

quiz.q: A ln n plot gives a slope of −8 per mm for τ = 1.5 h. Find G and L<sub>D</sub>.
n° = 2.0 × 10<sup>8</sup> per (m³ mm), G = 0.20 mm/h and τ = 5.0 h. Find n at L = 1.0 mm, B° and N<sub>T</sub>.
quiz.a: Gτ = 1.0 mm, so n = 2.0 × 10<sup>8</sup> × e<sup>−1</sup> = 7.36 × 10<sup>7</sup> per (m³ mm); B° = 4.0 × 10<sup>7</sup> per (m³ h); N<sub>T</sub> = 2.0 × 10<sup>8</sup> per m³.

quiz.q: With i = 3 and fixed magma density, by what factor do G and L<sub>D</sub> change if τ is doubled?
quiz.a: G ∝ τ<sup>−4/(i+3)</sup> = τ<sup>−2/3</sup>: G falls to 2<sup>−2/3</sup> = 0.63 of its value. L<sub>D</sub> ∝ τ<sup>(i−1)/(i+3)</sup> = τ<sup>1/3</sup>: it rises by 1.26. Doubling the vessel gives only 26 % larger crystals.

quiz.q: A ln n plot bends upward at the smallest sizes. Give two possible causes.
quiz.a: Breakage or attrition adds fragments at small sizes; small crystals may grow slower than large ones (size-dependent growth or growth-rate dispersion), so they accumulate.

beyond: Not for the exam. The population balance is now solved numerically for crystallizers with fines destruction, classification, breakage and agglomeration, and coupled to fluid flow simulations of the vessel. In-line laser and image probes measure the CSD during operation. Search for population balance modelling of crystallization and focused beam reflectance measurement.

figure.caption: The MSMPR worked example. Left: the four measured population densities fall on a straight line of ln n against L; its slope −5.0 per mm gives Gτ = 0.20 mm and its intercept gives n°. Right: the mass distribution L³e<sup>−L/Gτ</sup> that follows, peaking at the dominant size 0.60 mm, with 26.5 % of the mass above 1.0 mm.

spec.aria: Left, a straight line falling from ln n of 22.33 at zero size through four data points to 18.33 at 0.8 millimetres. Right, a skewed hump of product mass against size peaking at 0.60 millimetres, with the tail above 1.0 millimetre shaded.
